lemma_split_regular_crossed.statement: Let k be any field and G a finite group. Let L = k^G be the product of |G| copies of k indexed by G, with G acting by right translation. Then L is a Galois G-algebra over k, and the crossed product algebra (L,G,1) is isomorphic to M_{|G|}(k). In particular, over a field of characteristic p>2, M_{p^2}(k) is a crossed product algebra for G = C_p x C_p.
lemma_split_regular_crossed.proof: Let n=|G|. Regard L=k^G as the k-algebra of all functions x:G→k. For σ∈G define α_σ(x)(g)=x(gσ) for all g∈G. Then α_σ is a k-algebra automorphism of L, and α_σ α_τ=α_{σ τ}, because α_σ(α_τ(x))(g)=α_τ(x)(gσ)=x(gστ)=α_{σ τ}(x)(g). Hence L is a G-algebra. The elements e_g∈L, given by e_g(h)=δ_{g,h}, are orthogonal idempotents and L=∏_{g∈G} k e_g, so L is commutative etale and dim_k L=n=|G|. If x∈L^G, then x(gσ)=x(g) for all g,σ; for arbitrary g,h choose σ=g^{-1}h, so x(h)=x(gσ)=x(g), hence x is constant. Constants are fixed, so L^G=k. Thus L is a Galois G-algebra. Now let A=(L,G,1)=⊕_{σ∈G} L u_σ, with u_1=1, u_σ u_τ=u_{σ τ}, and u_σ x=α_σ(x)u_σ. The constant function 1 is a normalized 2-cocycle. Define ρ:A→End_k(L) by ρ(∑_{σ∈G} x_σ u_σ)(y)=∑_{σ∈G} x_σ α_σ(y). It is k-linear. For monomials x u_σ and y u_τ, ρ((x u_σ)(y u_τ))(z)=ρ(x α_σ(y) u_{σ τ})(z)=x α_σ(y) α_{σ τ}(z), while ρ(x u_σ)ρ(y u_τ)(z)=ρ(x u_σ)(y α_τ(z))=x α_σ(y α_τ(z))=x α_σ(y) α_{σ τ}(z). Thus ρ is a k-algebra homomorphism. Using the basis e_g of L, identify End_k(L) with M_n(k). For g,h∈G put E_{g,h}=e_g u_{g^{-1}h} e_h∈A. For t∈G, ρ(E_{g,h})(e_t)=ρ(e_g)ρ(u_{g^{-1}h})ρ(e_h)(e_t). Since ρ(e_h)(e_t)=e_h e_t=δ_{h,t}e_h, this is zero if t≠h. If t=h, then α_{g^{-1}h}(e_h)(s)=e_h(s(g^{-1}h)) is 1 exactly when s=g, so α_{g^{-1}h}(e_h)=e_g, and therefore ρ(E_{g,h})(e_h)=e_g. Hence ρ(E_{g,h}) is the matrix unit sending e_h to e_g and killing all other e_t. The image of ρ therefore contains all n^2 matrix units, so ρ is surjective. Since dim_k A=n·dim_k L=n^2 and dim_k End_k(L)=n^2, ρ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the inverse sends the matrix with entries a_{g,h} in the e_g basis to ∑_{g,h} a_{g,h} e_g u_{g^{-1}h} e_h. Thus (L,G,1)≅M_n(k). Finally take G=C_p x C_p. Then |G|=p^2, and the result gives (k^{C_p x C_p}, C_p x C_p, 1)≅M_{p^2}(k). Since 1 is a normalized 2-cocycle, this exhibits M_{p^2}(k) as a crossed product algebra for G. The characteristic hypothesis p>2 is not used in the construction, so the statement holds in particular over any field of characteristic p>2.

lemma_tensor_crossed.statement: Let k be a field. Let A_1=(L_1,G_1,c_1) and A_2=(L_2,G_2,c_2) be crossed product algebras over k. Suppose that, with G_1 acting on L_1 and trivially on L_2 and G_2 acting on L_2 and trivially on L_1, the tensor product L_1 tensor_k L_2 is a Galois (G_1 × G_2)-algebra over k. Then A_1 tensor_k A_2 is isomorphic to a crossed product algebra (L_1 tensor_k L_2, G_1 × G_2, c) for some 2-cocycle c:(G_1 × G_2)×(G_1 × G_2) → (L_1 tensor_k L_2)^×.
lemma_tensor_crossed.proof:
Proof. In this proof a 2-cocycle means a normalized twisted 2-cocycle: if L is a G-algebra, c:G×G→L^× satisfies c(1,g)=c(g,1)=1 and c(a,b)c(ab,d)=a(c(b,d))c(a,bd) for all a,b,d∈G. This is the identity forced by associativity in a crossed product. This is the convention under which the crossed product presentation is unital with u_1=1. If a different convention is used, one first passes to the equivalent normalized presentation; since the lemma is about isomorphism classes, and tensoring with isomorphisms preserves the isomorphism class of the tensor product, this preliminary normalization does not affect the result. Hence we may and do assume u_1=1 in A_1 and v_1=1 in A_2; the relations with one argument 1 then force c_1(1,g)=c_1(g,1)=1 and c_2(1,h)=c_2(h,1)=1, and c_1,c_2 satisfy the twisted cocycle identity.

Let u_g be the homogeneous basis element of A_1 and v_h the homogeneous basis element of A_2. Put L=L_1⊗_k L_2 and G=G_1×G_2, with (g,h) acting by (g,h)(x⊗y)=g(x)⊗h(y). By hypothesis L is a Galois G-algebra over k, so dim_k L=|G_1||G_2| and L^G=k. Set w_{(g,h)}=u_g⊗v_h in A=A_1⊗_k A_2. Since A_1=⊕_{g}L_1u_g and A_2=⊕_{h}L_2v_h, tensoring over k gives an L-vector space decomposition A=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}L w_{(g,h)}. The subalgebra L is the (1,1)-component. For x⊗y∈L, w_{(g,h)}(x⊗y)=(u_g⊗v_h)(x⊗y)=u_gx⊗v_hy=g(x)u_g⊗h(y)v_h=(g(x)⊗h(y))w_{(g,h)}=(g,h)(x⊗y)w_{(g,h)}. Define c:G×G→L^× by c((g,h),(g',h'))=c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'). This is a unit, with inverse c_1(g,g')^{-1}⊗c_2(h,h')^{-1}. For basis elements, w_{(g,h)}w_{(g',h')}=(u_g⊗v_h)(u_{g'}⊗v_{h'})=u_gu_{g'}⊗v_hv_{h'}=c_1(g,g')u_{gg'}⊗c_2(h,h')v_{hh'}=(c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'))(u_{gg'}⊗v_{hh'})=c((g,h),(g',h'))w_{(g,h)(g',h')}. The first relation was already checked on pure tensors and hence holds for all x∈L by linearity. Thus the elements w_{(g,h)} satisfy the two defining relations of the crossed product (L,G,c). It remains to check that c is a normalized twisted 2-cocycle. For a=(g,h), b=(g',h'), d=(g'',h'')∈G, we compute c(a,b)c(ab,d)=(c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'))(c_1(gg',g'')⊗c_2(hh',h''))=c_1(g,g')c_1(gg',g'')⊗c_2(h,h')c_2(hh',h''). On the other hand, a(c(b,d))c(a,bd)=((g,h)(c_1(g',g'')⊗c_2(h',h')))(c_1(g,g'g'')⊗c_2(h,h'h''))=(g(c_1(g',g''))⊗h(c_2(h',h'')))(c_1(g,g'g'')⊗c_2(h,h'h''))=g(c_1(g',g''))c_1(g,g'g'')⊗h(c_2(h',h''))c_2(h,h'h''). In this action term, g acts on the L_1-factor and h acts on the L_2-factor, the cross actions being trivial by hypothesis. Because c_1 is a twisted 2-cocycle for the G_1-action on L_1, it satisfies c_1(g,g')c_1(gg',g'')=g(c_1(g',g''))c_1(g,g'g''); because c_2 is a twisted 2-cocycle for the G_2-action on L_2, it satisfies c_2(h,h')c_2(hh',h'')=h(c_2(h',h''))c_2(h,h'h'). Therefore the first components of the two tensor products are equal and the second components are equal, so c(a,b)c(ab,d)=a(c(b,d))c(a,bd) for all a,b,d∈G. Normalization is also immediate: c((1,1),(g',h'))=c_1(1,g')⊗c_2(1,h')=1⊗1 and c((g,h),(1,1))=c_1(g,1)⊗c_2(h,1)=1⊗1. Now let B be the crossed product algebra (L,G,c), with homogeneous basis e_{(g,h)} and relations e_{(g,h)}x=(g,h)(x)e_{(g,h)}, e_{(g,h)}e_{(g',h')}=c((g,h),(g',h'))e_{(g,h)(g',h')}. The assignment x⊗y↦x⊗y on L and e_{(g,h)}↦w_{(g,h)} extends to a k-algebra homomorphism φ:B→A, by the universal property of the crossed product presentation, because the elements w_{(g,h)} satisfy exactly these relations. It is surjective, since A=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}Lw_{(g,h)}. To see that this decomposition is direct, note that u_g and v_h are units: u_gu_{g^{-1}}=c_1(g,g^{-1})u_1=c_1(g,g^{-1})1 and v_hv_{h^{-1}}=c_2(h,h^{-1})1, so multiplication by u_g (resp. v_h) is an isomorphism L_1→L_1u_g (resp. L_2→L_2v_h). Since A_1=⊕_{g}L_1u_g and A_2=⊕_{h}L_2v_h are finite direct sums, A=(⊕_{g}L_1u_g)⊗_k(⊕_{h}L_2v_h)=⊕_{g,h}(L_1u_g)⊗_k(L_2v_h), and each summand (L_1u_g)⊗_k(L_2v_h) is Lw_{(g,h)} via (a u_g)⊗(b v_h)=(a⊗b)w_{(g,h)}. Since L is a Galois G-algebra, dim_k L=|G|; hence dim_k A=|G|dim_k L=|G|^2. By definition, B=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}Le_{(g,h)}, so dim_k B=|G|dim_k L=|G|^2. Therefore φ is an isomorphism. Consequently A_1⊗_k A_2 is isomorphic to the crossed product algebra (L_1⊗_k L_2,G_1×G_2,c).
